items.headline: Auntie Vee's storage unit sells for C$40; the good stuff is missing
items.body: Astoria's most legendary collector retired to Florida and left eight treasures with friends around the neighborhood. Sal at the deli says he knows where to start. Join from Tasks, then Hunt. It ends Sunday at midnight.

items.headline: Chase Clout streams himself "touching grass" for nine hours at Astoria Park
items.body: Peak viewers: 41,000. Grass touched: one patch, repeatedly. Gus, who has sat on the same bench since 1987, appeared in frame for six of the nine hours and is now trending.

items.headline: Peyton Pastel unveils a pastel pumpkin spice line; pumpkins demand an apology
items.body: The latte is lavender, the muffin is mint and the candle smells like "an autumn you can trust." Her apology video is reportedly already filmed, just in case.

items.headline: Dunk Daniels arrives early to practice; teammates call security
items.body: Witnesses say he was "just standing there, on time, like a stranger." Sources close to the team believe his watch was set to the wrong time zone. It will not happen again.

items.headline: Ask Lola: "My ex will be at the party. Do I still go?"
items.body: "Babe, you go, you arrive forty minutes late, and you leave before the good song. Wear the outfit that makes the bouncer say 'oh.' You are not attending a party. You are attending a reminder." Lola Lowdown

items.headline: Skyler Beta launches an app to win treasure hunts; it sends everyone to the same bodega
items.body: Sal reports a 400% rise in chopped cheese sales and zero treasure found. Skyler calls it "a successful beta of the bodega vertical."

items.headline: Chardonnay Shade's spin-off pilot is 44 minutes of her ordering at Neon Spoon
items.body: Test audiences called it "tense" and "somehow about all of us." Network executives have ordered six more episodes and a second diner.

items.headline: Brock Squarejaw does his own stunt on the N train: standing without holding the pole
items.body: He lasted two stops. Commuters gave him a polite round of applause and one seat, which he refused "for the character."

items.headline: Lunaria plays a secret show at Velvet Static; nobody can prove it happened
items.body: Everyone who was there swears it changed their life. Nobody took a single photo. Rocco the bouncer confirms only that "the vibes were real" and that he will not be taking questions.

items.headline: Tiff lands her first brand deal: a single free coffee
items.body: The coffee was from Grind & Gossip. The deal was Jojo saying "fine, take it." Tiff has posted about it eleven times and calls herself "in partnership."

items.headline: Brick Tackleton's cooking show premieres; every dish is a protein shake
items.body: Episode one: breakfast (a shake). Episode two: dinner (a warmer shake). Critics praise his knife work, which was used only to open the shake.

items.headline: 7 train delays: a signal at Queensboro Plaza is "thinking about it"
items.body: Expect delays on the 7 in both directions this evening while crews talk a signal into turning green. The Metro Rail Authority thanks you for your patience, which it has never once deserved.

items.headline: N/W running slow: a train has entered a "mechanical mood"
items.body: Morning N and W trains are running with delays after one train refused to leave Astoria Blvd. Crews say it's "just tired." Same, honestly.

items.headline: MRA board votes to study whether to discuss a fare increase
items.body: After a four-hour meeting, the Metro Rail Authority board agreed to form a committee to decide whether to schedule a meeting about fares. Fares stay where they are. The snacks at the meeting were excellent.

items.headline: Weekend service: the 7 runs local to Flushing, every stop, no exceptions
items.body: This Saturday the 7 makes every stop between Long Island City and Flushing. Bring a snack, a podcast and the patience of a saint. The dumplings at the end are worth it.

items.headline: N/W rerouted on Sunday: trains take "the scenic route"
items.body: Track work sends Sunday N and W trains on a detour. The MRA calls it scenic. Riders call it a schlep. Allow extra time to reach Astoria.
